A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KG-synthetic relational-semantics study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-style and diffusion-model experiments, including memorization, relational generalization, layer-wise analyses, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds template-diversity, pretrained GPT-2, and compositional-relation results.

M1.justification: The original KG construction, GPT-style training, layer-wise probing, and LLaDA-style diffusion procedures remain unchanged. Section 6 extends the experimental settings without introducing a new algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Section 6.2 adds unseen-entity evaluation of father/father-to-grandfather composition, extending coverage beyond single-relation symmetry and inversion. This is a limited new reasoning task within the retained synthetic kinship domain.

E2.justification: Figure 8 and Appendix A.5 retain the same autoregressive and LLaDA-style diffusion comparators. Section 6.1 adds a GPT-2 initialization/adaptation study, including an unadapted control, rather than another comparison method.

E3.justification: v2 adds a template sweep at N = 10,000, pretrained GPT-2 continuation without QA SFT at N = 0–50,000, and compositional completion tests at N = 50,000 and 100,000. Table 4→6 also corrects the third documented ICL prompt from person_a to person_b; whether this reflects rerunning earlier experiments is unstated.

E4.justification: The new Table 1 tests whether template diversity remains necessary when training-sample coverage is sufficient. Section 6 adds focused checks of generality across pretrained initialization and compositional complexity. The existing appendix template, layer-wise, SFT-fraction, and diffusion analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 retains the statement that results ordinarily come from a single run. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Existing plotted results are retained. New Table 1 reports inversion/symmetry accuracies of 95.00%/97.00% at N = 10,000 and K = 10. Table 2 adds pretrained GPT-2 results, from 6.00%/8.00% without adaptation to 98.89%/99.32% at N = 50,000. Section 6.2 adds composition accuracy near 0% at N = 50,000 and 47.6% at N = 100,000.

T1.justification: The formal KG, corpus-generation, and SFT definitions in Appendix A.3 are unchanged. The grandfather-composition example specifies an additional empirical task; no new theoretical analysis, proof, or derivation is developed.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central claims about relational emergence, shallow-model capability, intermediate-layer signals, and autoregressive order bias. The conclusion is shortened, but its omitted layer-wise finding remains claimed elsewhere.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications that ICL success may involve shallow matching and that pretrained completion results do not establish transfer of the reversal-bias findings. It also interprets the new experiments in terms of template diversity and the greater data requirements of compositional relations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page code-repository link and states code availability, whereas v1 only promises release. Table 3→5 corrects a missing job relation and an inconsistent occupation in the generation example. Existing appendix hardware, hyperparameters, and training schedules are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to nostalgebraist's logit lens, Belrose et al.'s tuned lens, and Lin et al. on reversal generalization. These provide limited additional context for layer-wise interpretation and training-document effects without substantially redefining the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar, terminology, heading, contact-information, and cross-reference corrections. It inserts Result 4, expands discussion and limitations, and shortens the conclusion while retaining the existing narrative sequence.

P2.justification: v2 adds two main-text tables and renumbers the five existing appendix tables. Several figures move between columns, and Figure 5 is redrawn with its duplicated panel label corrected to (d). The existing figures and appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The template-diversity test and pretrained/compositional extensions provide useful additional evidence, while the new shortcut and applicability caveats improve interpretation. Code-access information and corrected examples also help reproducibility. The gains remain limited by single-run reporting and sparse documentation of the composition experiment; the retained limitation claiming no multi-hop compositional testing also conflicts with Section 6.2.
